Rashi on Yevamot 39b:10:2.english: Extend - Turn [your] right foot sideways toward her.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:11:1.english: That was visible to us - For we require spittle that is visible to the eyes of the judges, [as stated] in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Chalitzah (below, Yevamot 106b).

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:12:1.english: And I will have them recite - [Namely,] "I do not wish to take her."

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:13:1.english: Through witnesses - [Meaning] that one must bring two witnesses that he is the brother of the deceased from his father.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:15:1.hebrew: אכשור דרי - בתמיה, וכי נתכשרו הדורות:
Rashi on Yevamot 39b:15:1.english: Have the generations improved - [Said] in wonderment: Have the generations indeed become worthy?

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:18:1.english: Her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her — a mitzva - This is our reading. One does not read here "for a mitzva," rather [only] later, in the resolution of Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:18:2.english: As initially - before his brother betrothed her.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:18:3.english: She became forbidden - When his brother betrothed her.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:18:4.english: And she reverted and became permitted - When [his brother] died without children.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:18:5.english: [One] might [think] she would revert to her original permitted status - [The Gemara] explains [this] later.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:19:1.english: Who is the Tanna - And what is he saying?

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:19:2.hebrew: אבא שאול היא וה"ק יבמה יבא עליה למצוה - משמע לשם מצות יבום, דכתב ויבמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39b:19:2.english: It is Abba Shaul, and this is what [the baraita] is saying: "Her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her" [means] for a mitzva - [This] implies for the sake of the mitzva of levirate marriage, as it is written, "and perform levirate marriage with her."

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:21:1.hebrew: רבא אמר אפי' תימא רבנן - ולא תיתני "למצוה" אלא "מצוה":
Rashi on Yevamot 39b:21:1.english: Rava said: You [can] even say [it is in accordance with] the Rabbis - And do not teach [the baraita as] "for the mitzva" [lemitzvah], rather "a mitzva" [mitzvah].

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:21:2.english: "Her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her" — [it is] a mitzvah - [It is] a mitzvah for him to perform levirate marriage with her rather than chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:22:1.hebrew: יכול תחזור להיתירה הראשון - ותו לא, דאי בעי לא כניס לה. ת"ל "יבמה יבא עליה" — מצוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39b:22:1.english: One might [have thought] that she would revert to her original permitted status - And nothing more, [meaning] that if he wishes, he does not marry her. Scripture states: "Her brother-in-law shall cohabit with her" — [it is] a mitzvah.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:23:1.english: Will she be released for nothing - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:24:1.hebrew: מצות תאכל - קרא יתירא הוא, דכתיב ברישא דקרא "והנותרת מן המנחה יאכלו":
Rashi on Yevamot 39b:24:1.english: It shall be eaten unleavened - It is a superfluous [phrase], as it is written at the beginning of the verse: "And the remainder of the meal-offering they shall eat."

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:8:1.english: There we learned - In Tractate Bekhorot.

Rashi on Yevamot 39b:9:1.hebrew: אמר רב אין כופין - ואי ניחא לתרוייהו לייבומי, אין כופין אותו לחלוץ דנימא לאו למצוה מכווני ופגע באיסור אשת אח, אלא אי בעי מייבם. ומיהו, היכא דהוא צבי לייבומי ואיהי אמרה "לא בעינא ליה" ואמרה דברים ניכרים, אי מצינו לאטעוייה ולומר לו "חלוץ לה ע"מ שתתן לך מאתים זוז" — מטעינן ליה, ואי לא — כפינן ליה וחליץ, דאמר רב ששת (לעיל יבמות ד.): מנין ליבמה שנפלה לפני מוכה שחין שאין חוסמין אותה? ולא תימא מוכה שחין דוקא, אלא כל אמתלא שתתן לדבריה, דאמר בהמדיר (כתובות עז.): מעשה בציידן בבורסי שמת ולו אח בורסי, ואמרו חכמים: יכולה שתאמר "לאחיך הייתי יכולה לקבל, ולך איני יכולה לקבל". ועוד פסקינן הלכתא באע"פ (שם סד.): כותבין אגרת מרד על ארוסה, ואין כותבין אגרת מרד על שומרת יבם. ומכל הלין טעמי, כפינן ליה דחליץ ושקלה כתובה. וכל הני "אין כופין" דהכא — היכא דתרוייהו ניחא להו:
Rashi on Yevamot 39b:9:1.english: Rav said: We do not force - If both of them are willing to consummate the levirate marriage, we do not force him to perform chalitzah on the grounds that we might say they do not intend [to act] for the sake of the mitzvah and he is [thus] violating the prohibition of a brother's wife; rather, if he wishes, he consummates the levirate marriage. However, where he wants to consummate the levirate marriage, and she says, "I do not want him," and she gives substantive reasons: if we can trick him and say to him, "Perform chalitzah for her on condition that she gives you two hundred zuz," we trick him; and if not, we force him and he performs chalitzah, for Rav Sheshet said (above, Yevamot 4a): From where [do we derive] regarding a yevamah who fell [for levirate marriage] before one afflicted with boils that we do not muzzle her? And do not say [that this applies] specifically [to] one afflicted with boils, rather [to] any plausible reason that she gives for her statement, as it is stated in [the chapter] Hamadir (Ketubot 77a): There was an incident in Sidon involving a tanner who died and had a brother who was a tanner, and the Sages said: She can say, "Your brother I was able to tolerate, but you I cannot tolerate." And furthermore, we rule the halakhah in [the chapter] Af Al Pi (ibid. 64a): We write a document of rebellion against a betrothed woman, but we do not write a document of rebellion against a woman awaiting levirate marriage. And for all these reasons, we force him so that he performs chalitzah and she collects [her] ketubah. And all these [statements of] "we do not force" here [refer to] where both of them are willing.

Tosafot on Yevamot 39b:11:1.hebrew: דמתחזיא לן בבי דינא על ארעא - נראה דל"ג "על ארעא", דלא צריך, כדאמר בפרק מצות חליצה (לקמן יבמות דף קו: ושם) גבי "הוא ארוך והיא גוצא וקלטתו הרוח":
Tosafot on Yevamot 39b:11:1.english: Which was visible to us in the court upon the ground - It appears that we do not read [the words] "upon the ground," as it is unnecessary, as it states in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Chalitzah (later, Yevamot 106b, and there) regarding [the case where] "he is tall and she is short, and the wind caught it [the spittle]."

Tosafot on Yevamot 39b:17:1.hebrew: ולשום אישות - דתיפוק ליה עליה שם אישות. אר"י כי אין פירושו כההיא דבסמוך: "רצה לשם נוי — כונסה, רצה לשם אישות — כונסה", דההוא "לשם אישות" היינו לשם מצות יבום. וכה"ג איכא בפרק הבא על יבמתו (לקמן יבמות דף נג: ושם): "אפילו שניהם שוגגין או מזידים" — דההוא "מזיד" לשם זנות, ולא הוי כההוא דקאמר התם דרבי רחמנא ביאת שוגג כמזיד, דההוא "מזיד" במתכוין לשם מצוה; וכן "אפילו הוא שוגג והיא מזידה":
Tosafot on Yevamot 39b:17:1.english: Or for the sake of marital relations [ishut] - [Meaning] that the status of marital relations should take effect for him upon her. Rabbi Yitzchak said that its meaning [here] is not like that [statement] nearby: "If he wished [to marry her] for the sake of beauty, he marries her; if he wished [to marry her] for the sake of marital relations, he marries her," because that [phrase] "for the sake of marital relations" [there] means for the sake of the mitzvah of levirate marriage. And similarly, there is [an example] in the chapter [entitled] HaBa al Yevamto (below, Yevamot 53b and elsewhere): "Even if both of them are unwitting or intentional" — for that "intentional" [means] for the sake of licentiousness, and it is not like that [statement] that [the Gemara] says there, that the Merciful One included unwitting intercourse as [equivalent to] intentional [intercourse], for that "intentional" [refers to] one who intends for the sake of the mitzvah; and similarly [in the phrase], "even if he is unwitting and she is intentional."

Tosafot on Yevamot 39b:9:1.hebrew: אמר רב אין כופין - פירש בקונטרס כי ניחא לתרוייהו לייבם אין כופין לחלוץ משום מצוה דנימא דלאו למצוה מכווני, אבל אם לא תרצה לייבם מחמת שתתן אמתלא לדבריה, אם אין יכולין להטעותו, כפינן ליה וחליץ. וממוכה שחין ובורסי שהביא בקונט', נראה דאין ראיה, שהן מאותם שכופין להוציא מן הבעל; אבל בשאר אמתלא אין נראה לומר דכופין, דאל"כ, למה היו טורחין לקמן בפרק מצות חליצה (יבמות דף קו.) להטעותו? יכפוהו לחלוץ! ומאגרת מרד אין ראיה, דא"כ בלא אמתלא נמי; והתם הוי טעמא משום דמצות חליצה קודמת, כדמסיק. ועוד, דקאמר התם רבי יוחנן: "תבע לייבם אין נזקקין לו", השתא לחלוץ כופין, ואין נזקקין לייבם מבעיא?! ועוד, מדקאמר "בדידך תלה רחמנא", משמע אפי' בזמן הזה דמצות חליצה קודמת. ור"ת גריס: "מצות יבום קודמת למצות חליצה אמר רב אין כופין", וקאי אבראשונה שהיו מתכוונין לשם מצוה, וקאמר דאין כופין לייבם. וכי הוו אתו לקמיה דרב — אותן שהיו מתכוונים לשם מצוה. ורב יהודה נמי דאתקין "אי צבית לייבומי" — באותן שבאין לפנינו לחלוץ איירי, שאותן אם היו מייבמין היו מכוונים לשם מצוה, שהרי לא היו מתכוונים לשם נוי ולשם אישות, שלא היו חוששים לייבם אלא לחלוץ; אבל אחריני אין מניחין לייבם, אלא אדרבה כופין לחלוץ. ואר"ת דהלכה כאבא שאול, כסתם מתני' דבכורות (דף יג.), ולא כרמי בר חמא דאמר: "חזרו לומר דמצות ייבום קודמת כרבנן". ועוד, דבריש מכילתין אוקי מתניתין דפ"ק (דף ג. ושם) כאבא שאול, ובפרק בית שמאי (לקמן יבמות דף קט. ושם) תני בר קפרא: "לעולם ידבק אדם בחליצה" כאבא שאול, וסתמא דגמרא בפרק אע"פ (כתובות דף סד. ושם) כאבא שאול. ולעיל בשמעתין דמשמע דביאה עדיפא — במתכוין לשם מצוה איירי. ור"ח פסק כאן דמצות יבום קודמת, וחזר בו בפ' מצות חליצה, ופסק דמצות חליצה קודמת:
Tosafot on Yevamot 39b:9:1.english: Rav said: [The court] does not force - Rashi [the Kuntres] explained that when both of them are amenable to consummating the levirate marriage, [the court] does not force [him] to perform ḥalitza on account of the mitzva, such that we would say they do not have intent for the sake of the mitzva. However, if she does not want to consummate the levirate marriage because she gives a valid reason for her words, if they are unable to deceive him [into performing ḥalitza], we force him and he performs ḥalitza. But from [the cases of] one afflicted with boils and a tanner that he cited in Rashi [the Kuntres], it appears that there is no proof [for this], since those are among the ones whom [the court] forces to divorce [a wife] from the husband [in an ordinary marriage]; however, with any other valid reason, it does not appear [correct] to say that we force [him], for if so, why did they take the trouble below in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Chalitzah (Yevamot 106a) to deceive him? Let them force him to perform ḥalitza! And from [the law regarding] a letter of rebellion there is no proof [either], for if so, [we should force him] even without a valid reason; rather, there the reason is because the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence, as [the Gemara] concludes [there]. Furthermore, Rabbi Yoḥanan says there: "If he demanded to consummate the levirate marriage, [the court] does not attend to him." Now, if we even force [him] to perform ḥalitza, is there any need [to state] that we do not attend to him to consummate the levirate marriage?! Furthermore, from [the Gemara's] statement, "The Merciful One makes [the matter] dependent upon your [will]," it is implied [that this applies] even nowadays, when the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence. And Rabbeinu Tam reads [the text as follows]: "The mitzva of levirate marriage takes precedence over the mitzva of ḥalitza — Rav said: [The court] does not force." And [Rav's statement] refers back to "initially, when they would have intent for the sake of the mitzva," and he is saying that [the court] does not force [him] to consummate the levirate marriage. And "when they would come before Rav" [refers to] those who had intent for the sake of the mitzva. And Rav Yehuda also, who enacted [the wording], "If you desire to consummate the levirate marriage," is speaking of those who come before us to perform ḥalitza, for if those [men] were to consummate the levirate marriage, they would have intent for the sake of the mitzva, since they did not have intent for the sake of beauty or for the sake of marriage, as they were not concerned to consummate the levirate marriage, only to perform ḥalitza; however, others we do not allow to consummate the levirate marriage, rather, on the contrary, we force [them] to perform ḥalitza. And Rabbeinu Tam says that the halakha is in accordance with Abba Shaul, like the unattributed Mishnah in Bekhorot (13a), and not like Rami bar Ḥama, who said: "They reverted to saying that the mitzva of levirate marriage takes precedence, in accordance with the Rabbis." Furthermore, at the beginning of our tractate, [the Gemara] establishes the Mishnah of the first chapter (3a and ibid.) in accordance with Abba Shaul, and in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (below, Yevamot 109a and ibid.), Bar Kappara taught: "A person should always cling to ḥalitza," in accordance with Abba Shaul, and the unattributed Gemara in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 64a and ibid.) is in accordance with Abba Shaul. And above in our sugya, where it is implied that [levirate] cohabitation is preferable — it is speaking of one who has intent for the sake of the mitzva. And Rabbeinu Ḥananel ruled here that the mitzva of levirate marriage takes precedence, and he retracted [this] in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Chalitzah, and ruled that the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence.
